tasks.short: Keep personnel files complete for hires, leave, training, complaints, and reviews.

today.trigger: A document arrives by mail, Teams, or paper, or a hire, move, certificate, complaint, review, reclassification, or leave needs a file.
steps: Decide which employee and which part of the file the document belongs to.
Check it against the SharePoint list for that event, such as ID, contract, VCA, forklift certificate, or absence letters.
File it in AFAS Profit or on the SharePoint personnel site and mark the item.
Ask the manager, recruiter, or employee when a signature or a page is missing.
Pass grievances, warnings, and long-absence files to the HR business partner.
drudgery: Renaming scans and dropping them in the right AFAS folder.
Repeating the same completeness check from memory.
Searching mail for the signed copy that was already sent once.
today.time_sinks: The same check is done by hand for every event, and Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo still mix AFAS, SharePoint, mail, and paper.

lenses.faster: Naming, filing, and the first completeness pass disappear. The administrator opens only the items the checklist cannot close.
lenses.autonomous: A new document, or a nightly gap report from AFAS, starts the check without a reminder.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, Noordhaven would keep a complete file for every employee and for flex workers who stay through the season, including the certificates and leave papers that are skipped when the floor is busy.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses renaming scans. The work that remains is reading a real complaint or a hard function classification and getting it right.
lenses.options: Show each file as complete, complete with named gaps, or blocked, and list the documents that would close the gaps.
lenses.altitude: The administrator maintains the checklist and the exception log, and stops being the person who files each scan.
reach: HR business partner: assemble the non-medical absence file before a Wet verbetering poortwachter meeting.
Learning and development specialist: see which VCA, forklift, and food-safety certificates are already on file.
Payroll specialist: see that the leaver and contract documents are present before month close.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a complaint, a warning, or a function change is complete and fair, and whether an absence paper is the company's to hold or the arbodienst's.
tasks.pattern_why: Several systems feed one file, and a wrong folder matters later in a dismissal or a poortwachter check. The useful change is a prepared filing with a person approving anything sensitive before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: A document arrives, or an AFAS event is missing a required item.
steps: Match the document to an employee and to an event checklist: hire, leave, training, complaint, review, or function.
Propose the AFAS location and whether that checklist item would then be complete.
Hold grievances, warnings, function changes, and anything that looks medical.
After approval, file the routine item and record what is still missing.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator approves every complaint, warning, function change, and absence document. A routine certificate posts only when the employee number and the expiry date match.
data_needed: Required-document list per event, agreed with the HR business partners and, where it sets a privacy rule, the works council.
Retention period per document type, including ID copies and BSN.
AFAS employee number, current contract, and site.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS document history and a SharePoint exception list reviewed each morning.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit keeps the digital personnel file and can attach documents to HR workflows.
Studytube already records course completion and certificates, so those need not be re-filed from mail.
A model can propose a dossier type for a scan, with a person approving the sensitive types.

risks: A grievance or warning filed in the wrong place weakens a later dismissal file.
Absence papers can contain health data. Those stay with the arbodienst, not in a folder a manager can open.
A new filing rule that uses personnel data can need works council consent under WOR art. 27 and an AVG retention check.
Keeping full ID copies or the BSN longer than needed breaches data minimisation.
research_questions: In a sample of 30 files per site, what share of required documents is missing, mis-filed, or duplicated between AFAS and SharePoint?
Which document types does the HR director require a person to read before they count as filed?
How many administrator hours last month went to renaming and filing, versus reading grievances and classifications?
Does AFAS already have a document checklist on the hire and absence workflows that nobody uses?

tasks.short: Enter address, pay, absence, output, and leaver changes on the employee record.

today.trigger: An employee, manager, or payroll reports a change of address, earnings, absence, output, or an end of employment.
steps: Read the mail, form, or photo and find the person in AFAS.
Type the address, absence code, earnings figure, output note, or end date and reason.
Check the absence code against the CAO list and whether payroll has closed the period.
Mail payroll or the manager when the figure does not match.
drudgery: Retyping addresses and dates from mail and photos.
Looking up the right verzuim code.
Fixing rows that payroll sends back at month close.
today.time_sinks: Changes arrive late, in free text, from three sites, and a wrong end date or allowance is often found only when payroll closes.

lenses.faster: Retyping from mail disappears for a change that passes the checks. The administrator handles pay, termination, and anything the rules reject.
lenses.autonomous: An inbound mail or form creates a proposed AFAS mutation the same day, without waiting until someone clears the inbox.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every absence and leaver would be coded in the same week and in the same way in Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo, so verzuim and the 90-day figures can be trusted.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping addresses. The work that remains is the odd leaver and the pay line that does not match.
lenses.options: Show the AFAS code the message most likely means and the two nearest codes, with the effect of each on the open payroll period.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the mutation rules and the payroll exception queue, and stops typing routine changes.
reach: Payroll specialist: take a checked mutation queue instead of retyping the same changes at month close.
People analytics and HRIS analyst: use absence and leaver reasons coded the same way on all three sites.
HR business partner: start from a coded leaver reason instead of an unmarked mail.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding a termination reason, a pay figure that matches no rule, and any change that looks like it should not reach payroll.
tasks.pattern_why: The input is mostly free text and the output is a fixed set of AFAS fields with checks: postcode, absence code, and payroll period. A model can propose the fields. Rules decide what may post.

in_practice.trigger: A change message arrives, or a manager submits an absence or leaver form.
steps: Turn the message into proposed fields: address, absence, earnings, output, end date, and reason.
Check a Dutch address against the BAG, the absence code against the CAO list, and the date against the open payroll period.
Post only an address or a standard absence code that passes every check.
Queue pay, allowances, performance notes, and terminations for the administrator before payroll runs.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing on pay, allowances, or an end of employment posts without the administrator. An address change posts only when the employee confirms it in AFAS InSite or the BAG check passes and the source is known.
data_needed: Allowed absence codes and who may submit them.
Payroll period lock calendar.
Which staff at each site can sign in to InSite.
A rule that flex-worker hours stay on the agency portal.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS mutation log, with the source message id, and the payroll exception queue.

evidence.claim: AFAS InSite lets employees submit their own changes, including address, which removes retyping for staff who can log in.
A Dutch address can be checked against the Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen.
Free-text absence and leaver mails can be proposed as HR fields, with a person still approving pay and termination.

risks: A wrong end date, scale, or allowance posts into AFAS payroll and is paid.
A termination reason written too early becomes a record the company may have to defend at UWV or the kantonrechter.
Many warehouse and transport staff have no desk, so the free-text queue will stay large if InSite is desk-only.
Flex hours from the three agencies are not employee mutations. Writing them into the employee file mixes two employment relationships.
research_questions: Last month, what share of address, absence, and leaver notices arrived as a form, an InSite request, or free text?
How many corrections in the last three payroll closes traced to an HR-admin typing error?
What share of warehouse and driver staff can sign in to InSite today?
Which fields does payroll refuse to take without a person: end date, allowance, termination reason?

tasks.short: Update the HR system for hires, leavers, leave, transfers, and promotions.

today.trigger: A hire, leaver, leave, transfer, or promotion is agreed and must be recorded in AFAS.
steps: Open the AFAS workflow and create or change the contract, function, and org unit.
Copy dates and salary scale from the Recruitee offer or the manager's mail.
Attach the signed contract and the leave or settlement letters.
Check cost centre, scale, and dates before payroll or the site uses the record.
drudgery: Clicking the same AFAS workflow screens.
Copying the accepted offer across from Recruitee by hand.
Sending the record back because a cost centre or scale was empty.
today.time_sinks: Recruitee and AFAS do not share the event, so the same hire is typed twice, often after the person has already started.

lenses.faster: Copying the offer into AFAS and walking a standard workflow disappear. The administrator sees only events the rules block.
lenses.autonomous: An accepted offer, or a submitted leave, transfer, promotion, or leaver request, opens the matching AFAS workflow the same day.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every event would be in AFAS before it takes effect, including the small transfers between sites that nobody finishes today.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses clicking through the same screens. The work that remains is the settlement or the return to work that does not fit a template.
lenses.options: For a promotion, show the record on the old scale and on the new scale, with the allowance effect, before anything is written.
lenses.altitude: The administrator designs the event workflows and reviews the failures, and stops shepherding every standard event.
reach: Recruiter: drop the shadow start-date list once the AFAS hire opens from the accepted offer.
Payroll specialist: receive hires and leavers inside the period lock instead of by mail the day before.
Learning and development specialist: a promotion or transfer that updates the certificates the new function requires.

tasks.human_edge: Non-standard exits, settlements, and partial returns to work that the standard workflow cannot finish.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS already has these event workflows. The gap is required fields, a mapping from the Recruitee offer, and a block while the record is incomplete. That is rules and software, not a model in the loop.

in_practice.trigger: A Recruitee offer is accepted, or a manager submits a leave, transfer, promotion, or leaver request on a form.
steps: Start the matching AFAS workflow and fill it from the offer or the form.
Block completion while cost centre, CAO scale, dates, or leave type is empty.
Attach the documents the event checklist already holds.
Leave settlements, partial returns, and any cross-CAO move with the administrator.
in_practice.human_gate: A hire, promotion, or leaver cannot complete while a required field fails. The administrator finishes any event that is not on the standard list.
data_needed: Field mapping from a Recruitee offer to an AFAS contract.
CAO scale table and org units per site.
The list of event types that stay manual.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS workflow log, including which fields were blocked and who released them.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit workflows already record hiring, leaving, leave, transfer, and promotion when those processes are configured.
Recruitee holds the accepted offer that is retyped into AFAS today.
An ATS-to-HRIS hire feed is a known integration pattern. The CAO field mapping for Noordhaven is local work, and the size of the gain is unmeasured.

risks: A workflow that completes with the wrong CAO or an empty cost centre looks finished and is wrong.
A transfer that is really part of a reorganisation can be a works council matter, even when one record looks routine.
A bad Recruitee-to-AFAS mapping copies the wrong salary into the contract of record.
AFAS already does much of this, so the time saved may be small.
research_questions: Of the last 25 hires, leavers, and transfers, how many AFAS fields were typed even though they already sat on the Recruitee offer or a form?
How often is the AFAS record still incomplete on the person's first shift or last day?
Which events in the last year could not be finished on the standard workflow, such as a settlement, a partial return, or a move between sites?

tasks.short: Check applications against certificates, right to work, and other must-haves.

today.trigger: A recruiter asks the administrator to process new applications for a warehouse, driver, or office role.
steps: Open the candidate in Recruitee and read the CV and the certificates.
Check right to work, VCA, forklift certificate or code 95, shift availability, and whether the form is complete.
Set the pipeline stage and note the gaps for the recruiter.
Mail the candidate when a certificate or an ID is missing.
drudgery: Reading CVs that state the same certificates in different layouts.
Chasing a missing VCA card.
Retyping eligibility notes into the stage.
today.time_sinks: Peak season brings a pile of driver and order picker applications, and each certificate is checked by eye.

lenses.faster: The first read for certificates, licence, and right to work disappears. The person reviews the flagged line and decides.
lenses.autonomous: A new application in Recruitee starts the checklist before anyone is asked to open it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every application in the seasonal peak would be checked against the real must-haves, not only the ones the recruiter has time to open.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses skimming identical CVs for a VCA date. The recruiter keeps the conversation with the candidate.
lenses.options: Show three readings side by side: meets the stated must-haves, missing a named item, or does not meet a stated must-have. No single score.
lenses.altitude: The administrator and the recruiter maintain the must-have list per role, and stop re-reading each CV for the same items.
reach: Recruiter: spend interview slots on people who already meet the certificate and right-to-work bar.
Learning and development specialist: see a certificate gap before day one rather than at the next audit.

tasks.human_edge: Any rejection, and any decision to proceed when the CV and the must-have list do not line up cleanly.
tasks.pattern_why: Knock-out items such as VCA, code 95, and right to work can be extracted and compared with the vacancy. Rejecting a person is a decision with discrimination and EU AI Act exposure, so a person changes the stage.

in_practice.trigger: A new application lands in a Recruitee vacancy that HR administration supports.
steps: Extract stated certificates, licence, right to work, and availability into a fixed checklist.
Compare that list with the vacancy must-haves only.
Propose one of three labels, each tied to a line in the application: complete, missing a named item, or does not meet a stated must-have.
Leave the stage change to the administrator or the recruiter.
in_practice.human_gate: No candidate is rejected or moved forward by the model. A person confirms the checklist before the Recruitee stage changes, and only a stated must-have may be a knock-out.
data_needed: Must-have list per vacancy, owned by the recruiter.
Which certificates are knock-outs and which are trained after hire.
A hard rule that age, gender, origin, and photo are not inputs.
in_practice.logs_to: A Recruitee stage note and a short decision log the recruiter can show the works council.

evidence.claim: Recruitee stores applications, vacancy data, and pipeline stages the checklist can read.
Licence and certificate checks are rule-like when the vacancy states them as must-haves. Reading them out of messy CVs is the model step.
Tools that select or rank candidates for employment can fall in the high-risk category of the EU AI Act.

risks: A model that scores fit, rather than a stated certificate, can discriminate and can be a high-risk employment system under the EU AI Act.
Certificate names vary, such as VCA, VCA-VOL, code 95, and forklift. A false reject loses a hire in peak season.
A knock-out that uses age, gender, or language as a proxy breaches the Algemene wet gelijke behandeling.
The recruiter owns the hiring decision. A tool that rejects on its own splits that accountability.
research_questions: Last quarter, what share of applications failed a fixed must-have, and what share needed a real judgment?
In a back-test, would any suggested reject have removed someone who was later hired and still here at 90 days?
Has the works council been consulted, and has the checklist been classified under the EU AI Act, given that a person still decides?

tasks.short: Answer staff questions on exams, eligibility, pay, and benefits.

today.trigger: An employee, shift lead, or manager asks about an exam, eligibility, salary, leave, or a benefit.
steps: Look the person up in AFAS for scale, contract, and leave balance.
Find the CAO clause or the SharePoint policy that fits.
Check Studytube when the question is about VCA, forklift, or food safety.
Reply, or pass a dispute to the HR business partner or to payroll.
drudgery: Answering the same shift-allowance and leave questions.
Searching SharePoint for the current CAO summary.
Being interrupted all day on Teams and on the floor.
today.time_sinks: The answers already sit in AFAS and in the CAO texts, but staff wait on one of two administrators, including for afternoon and night shifts.

lenses.faster: Searching the policy and the person's leave balance or certificate disappears when one approved source answers the question. Disputes and gaps stay with the administrator.
lenses.autonomous: The question itself is the trigger. A sourced reply goes back without an administrator on the clock, or the question escalates.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, a shift worker in Venlo or Tilburg would get a sourced answer on leave, allowance, and certificates during the shift, not the next morning.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the tenth ploegentoeslag question of the day. An eligibility case that does not fit the text is still a person's job.
lenses.options: When the CAO text has two readings, show both passages and say which one payroll currently applies. Do not pick a third reading.
lenses.altitude: The administrator curates the approved answers and the escalation rules, and stops being the live FAQ.
reach: HR business partner: stop being the second stop for routine scale and leave questions.
Payroll specialist: fewer 'what will this shift pay' mails in the week of month close.
Compensation and benefits specialist: only the questions that are real exceptions to the CAO text.
Learning and development specialist: exam status answered from Studytube instead of from an inbox.

tasks.human_edge: CAO disputes, complaints, and any question where the approved text does not fit that person's contract or site.
tasks.pattern_why: The question is free text. A safe answer is either a cited policy passage or a value read from an AFAS or Studytube field. The workflow must refuse to answer when no source matches.

in_practice.trigger: A question arrives by Teams, mail, or AFAS InSite about exams, eligibility, pay, benefits, or leave.
steps: Class the question as policy, as this employee's own figures, or as a dispute.
For policy, answer only with the SharePoint or CAO passage attached.
For figures, read leave balance, scale, and certificate status from AFAS and Studytube and show the field name.
Escalate when no passage matches, when the person disputes the figure, or when the question is a complaint.
in_practice.human_gate: A reply may go out only with its source attached. Anything without a source, anything that would change pay, and any complaint goes to the administrator.
data_needed: A short approved set of CAO and policy answers for the questions staff actually ask.
The AFAS fields the bot may read, by role of the asker.
The escalation path to payroll and the HR business partner.
in_practice.logs_to: A question log in Teams or InSite that stores the source passage and follows the AVG retention rule.

evidence.claim: AFAS InSite can show employees their own HR data, such as leave, which answers part of this queue without a mail.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can answer from the organisation's own SharePoint content.
A usable answer bot for CAO questions still needs a fixed source text and a refusal when that text does not cover the case.

risks: A fluent wrong answer on ploegentoeslag or pension is worse than a slow mail, because the employee may rely on it.
A personal answer in Teams can expose another worker's data if the role check fails.
A bot that reads the personnel file needs a DPIA and works council consent on the personnel-data rules before it is switched on.
Afternoon and night shifts will not use a bot that only works at a desk.
research_questions: What are the 20 most common questions, and for how many does one current CAO or policy passage give the whole answer?
How often was a written HR answer later corrected by payroll or an HR business partner?
Will shift staff in Tilburg and Venlo use Teams or InSite, or do they ask the shift lead?
Which AFAS fields may a bot read under the current authorisations?

tasks.short: Prepare the contract pack and put the new hire into the systems.

today.trigger: A manager and a recruiter decide to hire, and the candidate accepts the offer in Recruitee.
steps: Build the contract from the SharePoint template for the right CAO, site, and term.
Collect ID, BSN, loonheffingsverklaring, bank account, and certificates.
Create the employee and the contract in AFAS, and enrol the day-one courses in Studytube.
Send the pack for signature and file the signed copy.
drudgery: Copying the offer into Word and then into AFAS.
Chasing ID and bank details before day one.
Rebuilding the same starter checklist for every order picker.
today.time_sinks: Each hire is built as a fresh pack even when the role and the CAO are the same, and gaps show up at the gate on day one.

lenses.faster: Drafting the standard contract and the AFAS and Studytube drafts disappears. The person keeps the legal check and the identity check.
lenses.autonomous: An accepted offer in Recruitee opens the pack. The administrator is called when the draft is ready, not to start from a blank template.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, every hire, including the seasonal wave, would have a correct pack and the mandatory courses ready before day one.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding the same contract. Meeting someone at the gate with a file that is already right is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: When earlier agency time puts the person near the limit on successive fixed-term contracts, prepare both the fixed-term draft and the indefinite draft for a person to choose.
lenses.altitude: The administrator owns the templates and the release check, and stops assembling each pack from a blank page.
reach: Recruiter: hand over an accepted offer without rebuilding the starter list.
Learning and development specialist: day-one enrolment already drafted for VCA, forklift, or food safety.
Payroll specialist: a hire record that exists before the first shift.

tasks.human_edge: The hire decision stays with the manager and the recruiter. The administrator owns scale, proeftijd, the chain of fixed-term contracts, and the identity check against the original document.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack crosses Recruitee, Word, AFAS, and Studytube, and it becomes the contract of record. A draft can be assembled by software. It counts only after a person releases it.

in_practice.trigger: The offer is marked accepted in Recruitee.
steps: Select the contract template for the CAO, site, term, and function.
Fill name, hours, scale, proeftijd, and start date from the offer, and flag the proeftijd or the contract chain when it looks outside the rule.
Prepare the AFAS employee and the Studytube day-one enrolment as drafts.
Track ID, BSN, loonheffingsverklaring, and bank details on one list until they arrive.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator checks scale, term, proeftijd, and the contract chain, and only then releases the contract. A person checks identity against the original document. The AFAS hire does not complete before both checks.
data_needed: Current templates per CAO, approved by legal.
Scale placement rules for warehouse and transport functions.
Earlier contracts for this person, including agency time where that counts for the ketenregeling.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS contract workflow and the Recruitee offer record.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can generate employment contracts from templates and record the hire.
Recruitee holds the accepted offer that the contract is built from.
Studytube can enrol a person on a course. Pointing that enrolment at the hire event is local configuration.
Proeftijd length and the chain of fixed-term contracts are legal checks a template fill does not replace.

risks: A proeftijd that breaks the statutory maximum is void. A broken chain of fixed-term contracts can make the contract indefinite, including after agency time.
The identity check cannot be handed to a model. The employer still verifies the original document.
Releasing the draft too early sends an offer the company did not intend.
Storing a full ID copy for convenience conflicts with AVG data minimisation.
research_questions: In the last 20 hires, how many contracts had a wrong scale, proeftijd, hours, or CAO?
What is the median number of days from accepted offer to a complete AFAS employee and a Studytube enrolment?
For people who came in through a staffing agency, how often does earlier service change the contract that may be offered?
Who is allowed to release the contract today: the administrator, the recruiter, or the manager?

tasks.short: Look up the employee file and answer a question for a personnel decision.

today.trigger: An HR business partner, payroll, a manager, or the employee asks for something from the personnel file.
steps: Check that the asker is allowed to know it.
Search AFAS and the SharePoint dossier.
Copy the dates, scale, letters, or certificate status into a reply.
Refuse or redact when the question touches medical information.
drudgery: Opening a full file to answer a one-line question.
Hunting a warning letter filed under the wrong event.
Explaining again which absence facts the company may see.
today.time_sinks: The file is split between AFAS, SharePoint, and mail, so a simple question becomes a search across all three.

lenses.faster: Opening the file and copying dates into a mail disappears when the asker's role may see those fields. Sanction, dismissal, and medical requests stay with the administrator.
lenses.autonomous: The question triggers a role-checked lookup. Routine facts return with their source, without a meeting.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, the file for a poortwachter or performance conversation would be ready the hour it is asked for, so the meeting is not postponed for a search.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses digging for a contract end date. Deciding what a manager is allowed to see is the part that stays.
lenses.options: Return the short cited answer and, beside it, the list of items withheld because of role or because they are medical.
lenses.altitude: The administrator maintains who may see which section, and reviews the sensitive requests, and stops searching for routine facts.
reach: HR business partner: walk into a case with the dates and letters already cited.
Payroll specialist: contract end date and allowance basis without a dossier mail.
Compensation and benefits specialist: scale history for one person without asking for an export.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what this asker may see, and answering anything that will be used for a sanction, a dismissal, or a dispute.
tasks.pattern_why: The question is free text and the answer is a small set of fields or document dates that can be checked against AFAS. The workflow must enforce the role and stop on medical or disciplinary requests.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised person asks a factual question about one employee.
steps: Check the asker's AFAS role against the section they asked for.
Pull only the fields and document dates that answer that question.
Reply with those citations.
Stop when the request mentions health, a sanction, or a dismissal, or when the role does not match.
in_practice.human_gate: Medical data and the company doctor's re-integration view never leave the arbodienst channel. Requests that support a sanction or a dismissal are answered by the administrator.
data_needed: A role matrix: employee, manager, HR business partner, payroll, and what each may see.
A split between operational verzuim data and medical data.
A document index with event type and date.
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS audit trail of who saw which section, and why.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds the employee dossier with role-based access and an audit trail.
A retrieval step can return cited fields from a structured HR record instead of a forwarded PDF.
The employer's absence file has to stay separate from medical data held by the occupational health service.

risks: A helpful search that returns the whole file to a shift lead breaches AVG purpose limitation.
Mixing the company doctor's medical view into an employer answer breaches the poortwachter split.
An automatic answer pasted into a dismissal file will be read as the company's statement.
Copying dossier text into a chat log creates a second file with weaker control.
research_questions: Last month, what share of file questions were a single field, such as scale, end date, certificate, or FTE, versus a sanction or dismissal pack?
Does the current AFAS role model stop a shift lead from opening another worker's absence file, and is that access logged?
In a sample of replies, how many touched information that should have stayed with the arbodienst?

tasks.short: Chase other departments for personnel documents that are still missing.

today.trigger: A checklist for a hire, an absence, a review, or an audit shows a document that is not in the file.
steps: Mail or Teams the manager, the employee, or the other department.
Track who was asked and what is still open, often in a private Excel.
File what comes back into AFAS or SharePoint.
Escalate to the HR business partner when a site does not respond.
drudgery: Writing the same reminder again.
Keeping a private Excel of outstanding items.
Finding out on day one, or at audit, that the document was never sent.
today.time_sinks: Most of the elapsed time is waiting, and the next reminder depends on the administrator remembering to send it.

lenses.faster: Writing and tracking routine reminders disappears. The administrator spends time on silence after the last reminder, and on sensitive cases.
lenses.autonomous: An empty checklist item, or a certificate inside 60 days of expiry, starts the reminder cycle on its own.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost, nothing required would be missing at day 90 or at audit, because the chase would start the hour the gap appears.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the reminder mail. The call to a manager who is stuck, or who refuses, is the part that stays.
lenses.options: Give each gap a normal reminder path and a do-not-chase path that escalates at once for illness and grievances.
lenses.altitude: The administrator sets who owns each document and when to escalate, and stops keeping the chase list in their head.
reach: Learning and development specialist: one expiry list for forklift, VCA, and food safety, instead of a separate chase.
Recruiter: missing right-to-work documents chased on a clock before the start date.
HR business partner: only the stalled cases, not every reminder.

tasks.human_edge: The conversation when a site pushes back, and the judgment that a reminder is the wrong move, as with illness or a conflict.
tasks.pattern_why: Who to ask, when to remind, and when to escalate can be written down. A model is not required. The other person still has to supply the document, which is why the waiting does not disappear.

in_practice.trigger: A checklist item is still empty one day after the event, or a mandatory certificate expires within 60 days.
steps: Create a task for the named owner in Teams or Outlook: employee, manager, learning and development, or the agency contact.
Remind on a fixed schedule and show the open list per site.
File the reply when it matches the checklist item.
Escalate to the HR business partner on the morning the cycle ends with nothing usable.
in_practice.human_gate: The administrator steps in when the cycle ends, when the sender disputes the request, or when the document is a grievance or a medical paper. The workflow never treats a gap as filled without the document.
data_needed: The owner of each document type.
Reminder timing the managers have agreed to.
Which items Studytube, Recruitee, or an agency portal already holds, so nobody is chased for those.
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint outstanding-documents list per site, written back to the AFAS checklist.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Power Automate can send scheduled reminders from a list and escalate when a due date passes.
Studytube already stores certificate completions, so those items should not be chased by mail.
A reminder cycle only shortens the wait if managers and employees actually respond. That response is unmeasured here.

risks: Automatic reminders to someone on long-term sick leave can be the wrong tone and the wrong channel.
Chasing a certificate that Studytube or the agency already holds creates duplicates and annoys the site.
A manager who mutes the reminders leaves the file incomplete while the list looks under control.
Turning reply speed into a score on managers would be a monitoring change and needs works council care.
research_questions: Of the elapsed time on missing documents, what share is waiting on a named person, and what share is the administrator's own handling?
What share of chased items already exist in Studytube, Recruitee, or an agency portal?
In a four-week trial, do sites return documents faster on a fixed cycle than on ad-hoc mail, and how many people mute it?

role.altitude: The two administrators stop being the people who retype events and chase paper. They own the quality of personnel administration for three sites: the checklists, the release gates, the access rules, and the exception patterns payroll and the HR business partners can trust.
reach: Recruiter: first-pass certificate and right-to-work checks before an interview slot is used.
Payroll specialist: a mutation and hire queue that month-end can take without retyping.
Learning and development specialist: mandatory VCA, forklift, and food-safety enrolment and expiry chasing started from the hire and the certificate date.
HR business partner: a complete non-medical absence and case file before the conversation, without taking the conversation.
Compensation and benefits specialist: scale and allowance mismatches flagged against the CAO, without setting the policy.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks are about 45% of the role year. Two people cover Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo, plus a seasonal flex population that lives partly in three agency portals. Shift staff often have no desk, so self-service will not absorb every change. Grievances, dismissal files, poortwachter judgments, identity checks, and CAO disputes stay with a person. The works council and the AVG set the pace for any new use of personnel data. The north star, a hire who is productive and still here at 90 days, depends more on managers and recruiters than on faster filing.
skills_to_grow: AFAS workflow and required-field design, tested on one dummy employee per CAO.
AVG retention, role-based dossier access, and keeping medical data with the arbodienst.
The transport CAO and the warehouse CAO: contract type, proeftijd, allowances, and leave types.
Writing a gate: what may post on its own, what waits for a person, and how the exception is logged.
EU AI Act literacy and the works council route before any tool scores candidates or answers staff from the file.
role.ambitious_version: Every employee, and every flex worker who stays through the season, has a complete file before day one. Every mandatory certificate is valid. Every absence file shows the poortwachter dates. A manager on a night shift in Venlo gets a cited answer during the shift. The two administrators spend the week on the exceptions, the CAO edge cases, and on tightening rules the works council has agreed.
